media.title: Motion Picture Daily, 27 October 1934 — Kaper and Jurmann depart for MGM
media.description: Clipping from the “Purely Personal” column in Motion Picture Daily, 27 October 1934, p. 2. It reports Walter Jurmann (“Jourmann” in the item) and Bronisław Kaper (“Bron Kaper”) in New York with their wives, awaiting departure for the West Coast to begin work for M-G-M.
media.altText: Newspaper clipping reporting that Walter Jurmann and Bronisław Kaper were preparing to leave New York for MGM in California.

timelineEvents.title: MGM markets Kaper and Jurmann as “Viennese composers”
timelineEvents.label: MGM’s “Viennese” label
timelineEvents.shortDescription: American studio publicity recast Kaper and Jurmann as a Viennese composing team, turning “Vienna” into a promotional brand rather than a biographical fact.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Soon after their arrival at MGM, the American press and studio publicity presented Kaper and Jurmann as “Viennese composers” and as a brilliant Viennese musical team. The label suited MGM’s first use of the duo in Escapade, a Hollywood remake of the Viennese film Maskerade, but it was biographically misleading for Kaper, whose career had developed in Warsaw and Berlin. The event marks the moment when Hollywood began to translate his European professional history into a marketable studio identity.
